owner_posts.post_text:
Not every normal delivery progresses smoothly till the end. In some cases, labour advances well but the baby does not deliver despite good contractions. When the cervix is fully open and the baby’s head is already low, vacuum assisted delivery may be used to help complete the birth safely. This is a form of assisted delivery used only under specific conditions.

During vacuum delivery, a suction cup is attached to the baby’s head and gentle assistance is given while the mother pushes with contractions. This helps reduce prolonged strain during the second stage of labour and allows timely delivery when support is needed.

At Pradnya Maternity IVF and Multispeciality Hospital in Mulund, Dr Pradnya Randive manages labour and delivery with careful assessment at every stage. The focus is on safe normal delivery, early identification of delivery delays, and using assisted methods only when they are medically appropriate for the mother and baby.

Heavy Periods & Painful Periods Should Not Be Ignored

Many women experience heavy bleeding during periods, severe cramps, or both, and assume it is normal. However, when periods last more than 7 days, involve passing large clots, or require frequent pad changes, this condition is called menorrhagia. When periods are extremely painful and interfere with daily activities, it is known as dysmenorrhea.

According to Dr. Pradnya Randive, Obstetrician Gynaecologist and Fertility Specialist at Pradnya Maternity IVF & Multispeciality Hospital, Mulund, these symptoms often have underlying medical causes such as fibroids, endometriosis, pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), or thyroid-related problems. Ignoring them can lead to anaemia, fertility issues, and long-term health complications.

Early consultation with a gynaecologist helps identify the cause through basic evaluations such as blood tests and pelvic sonography, allowing timely and effective treatment. Not all heavy or painful periods require surgery, but they do require proper medical assessment.

At Pradnya Maternity IVF & Multispeciality Hospital, women receive personalised care for menstrual problems, pregnancy, and normal delivery, with a focus on accurate diagnosis and safe treatment.

If you are facing heavy bleeding, painful periods, or irregular cycles, consult a gynaecologist early and avoid self-medication.

featured_reviews.name: Gurprit Gill
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am deeply disappointed and frustrated by my experience at this fertility clinic.

I first visited the clinic in February 2026 based on a recommendation from a close friend. After witnessing everything we have endured over the past several months, that friend now regrets recommending the clinic in the first place.

From the outset, we made it absolutely clear that our goal was to proceed with IVF treatment. Initial test results were described as positive, yet we were told that a cyst needed to be removed before moving forward. Trusting the medical advice provided, we underwent surgery and completed a full course of costly medications. However, instead of progressing toward IVF as expected, we were placed on additional medications for nearly two more months with little to no explanation of how this was advancing our treatment plan.

By May, after repeatedly requesting clarity and asking why IVF had still not begun, estrogen tablets and other hormone medications were prescribed. A Serum E2 test was then performed while these medications were being taken. We were informed that the E2 level was high and were instructed to continue medication for another month. The exact same pattern occurred again during the June cycle: hormone medications continued, another E2 test was conducted, the result was again described as high, and treatment was postponed yet another time with more medications prescribed.

What is most troubling is the persistent lack of transparency and communication. Critical information is rarely explained clearly during consultations. Instead, patients are expected to return for multiple appointments to obtain answers that should have been provided openly and proactively. Despite significant waiting times at each visit, straightforward explanations and clear guidance remain difficult to obtain.

From February through the end of June, five valuable months passed without any meaningful progress toward the IVF treatment we originally sought. During that time, we experienced a continuous cycle of delays, repeated testing, additional medications, and postponed treatment milestones. On one occasion, treatment was delayed even further because the doctor was unavailable.

Fertility treatment is one of the most emotionally, physically, and financially challenging journeys a person can undertake. Patients place enormous trust in their healthcare providers and deserve honesty, transparency, timely communication, and a clearly defined treatment strategy. Unfortunately, our experience fell far short of those expectations. We invested months of time, significant financial resources, and considerable emotional energy into this process, yet received very little clarity regarding our actual progress toward IVF.

Based on our experience, I strongly encourage prospective patients to ask detailed questions, insist on clear explanations for every delay or change in treatment, and seriously consider obtaining a second opinion before committing to a long-term treatment plan at this clinic.
